monsters.name: Bat
monsters.pageRef: Bat [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Bat (SRD 5.1); Bat (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A cave roof, belfry or hollow tree, shared with hundreds more of its kind.

description.text: A hand-sized insect hunter that navigates a pitch-dark cavern by sound alone and never touches a wall doing it. One is harmless. A roost disturbed at dusk is a wall of them coming out at once, which is worth a Fright Check and nothing else.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (14): 1d-7 cutting, Reach C. Barely a wound; the bat is a nuisance and a disease vector, not a threat.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/bat.gct
Independent build total: -101 points of racial traits plus 5 points of racial skills.

Answers the SRD heading(s): Bat (SRD 5.1); Bat (SRD 3.5). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
Body mass used to scale this build: 0.03 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
Movement: ground Move 2; air Move 12 (primary). The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
Longest dimension about 25 cm with the wings out, which is the published table's SM -5 row.
ST is the floor: 30 g of animal carrying nothing but itself.
Perception is only moderately raised. The bat's edge is not general alertness but one extraordinary sense, and Scanning Sense, Ultrahearing and Acute Hearing 4 are where that is paid for.
Ground Move is deliberately crippled: a bat on the floor drags itself.

monsters.name: Blood Hawk
monsters.pageRef: Blood Hawk [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Blood Hawk (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A stick nest on a cliff ledge, ringed with the bones of whatever the flock last brought down.

description.text: A red-eyed raptor with none of a hawk's caution, hunting in flocks that mob anything warm-blooded crossing open ground. Individually one is a bird. Five arriving out of the sun, all going for the same face, is how travellers lose an eye.

attacks.name: Talons
attacks.notes: Talons (15): 1d-4 cutting, Reach C. Struck on the stoop, at the eyes and scalp. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Beak
attacks.notes: Beak (15): 1d-6 piercing, Reach C.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/blood-hawk.gct
Independent build total: -81 points of racial traits plus 2 points of racial skills.

Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
Body mass used to scale this build: 1.5 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
Movement: ground Move 2; air Move 12, 18 at a sprint (primary). The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
Body about 60 cm; Size Modifier follows body length, not the wingspan, because the wings fold.
ST from Basic Lift: it can carry roughly its own 1.5 kg for a short flight.
Will is high for a bird of this size and that is the point of the creature — it commits to a target that could kill it.

monsters.pageRef: Crab [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Crab (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A wet crevice under a rock at the tide line.

monsters.name: Crocodile
monsters.pageRef: Crocodile [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Crocodile (SRD 5.1); Crocodile (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A mud bank above a slow river, with a scraped nest hollow and a slide worn down into the water.

description.text: Four metres of armoured patience lying as a log until the moment it is not. It takes prey at the water's edge, drags it in, and drowns it, and its hide turns a spear that would go through anything else this side of a dragon. Out of the water it is slow. In the water nothing is winning.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 2d-2 cutting, Reach C. Closes and holds; the crocodile does not let go to bite again.

attacks.name: Death Roll
attacks.notes: Death Roll: Reach C. Against a target it already has in its jaws, the crocodile rolls its whole body. No attack roll; the victim rolls ST or DX to break the grip or is dragged under and drowned.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/crocodile.gct
Independent build total: -28 points of racial traits plus 18 points of racial skills.

Answers the SRD heading(s): Crocodile (SRD 5.1); Crocodile (SRD 3.5). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
Body mass used to scale this build: 350 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
Movement: ground Move 5; water Move 5, 7 at a sprint (primary). The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
Four metres nose to tail puts it on the SM +2 row. Length, not mass, is what the published table reads.
ST from Basic Lift: it drags an 80 kg carcass into the water, which is the job its strength has to do.
DR is full armour rather than Tough Skin: osteoderms are bone plates, not thick hide.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision; Rapid Healing; Resistant To Disease; the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Sea Horse
monsters.pageRef: Giant Sea Horse [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Giant Sea Horse (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: Kelp forest and reef shallows, anchored by the tail to whatever holds still.

description.text: Ridden by sea elves and sahuagin alike, and worth more than a good horse. It is armoured in bony rings, placid to the point of stubbornness, and slower than anything that wants to eat it — which is why it is a mount and not a hunter.

attacks.name: Ram
attacks.notes: Ram (13): 1d+2 crushing, Reach C. Driven with the whole body; the armoured snout is the only part of it built to hit anything.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/giant-sea-horse.gct
Independent build total: -39 points of racial traits plus 1 points of racial skills.
Answers the SRD heading(s): Giant Sea Horse (SRD 5.1). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
Body mass used to scale this build: 180 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
Movement: ground Move 3; water Move 3 (primary). The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
Three metres from crown to curled tail, which is the SM +1 row.
ST is set by what a mount has to do: Basic Lift must carry an armed rider. That raised it from an earlier draft, where it had been scaled from mass and could not have borne one.
Deliberately slow: Basic Move is bought down, because a sea horse's whole body plan trades speed for armour and station-keeping.
Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.pageRef: Giant Toad [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Giant Toad (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A wallow under a rotting log at the edge of standing water.

description.text: A toad the size of a hound, sitting so still in the reeds that it reads as a stone until the tongue comes out. It eats anything it can get into its mouth, which at this size includes a halfling, and its skin sweats a poison that punishes anyone who grabs it.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (14): 1d-2 crushing, Reach C. The toad swallows what it can and works on the rest.

attacks.name: Tongue
attacks.notes: Tongue (14): 1d-3 crushing, Reach C,1. Lashes out a hex, sticks, and drags a lighter target into reach of the mouth.

attacks.name: Toxic Skin
attacks.notes: Toxic Skin: Reach C. Anything that bites or grapples the toad bare-handed rolls HT or is nauseated and blurred of vision for minutes. No attack roll; contact alone does it.

description.text: Black dragons keep to swamp and drowned ruin, and they are the meanest of the chromatic line: cruel for its own sake, patient about it, and happy to let a place rot around them. The breath is acid, and it keeps working after it lands. A young dragon has its full growth ahead of it and its confidence already complete, which is the combination that gets villages burned over an insult nobody meant.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (13): 4d-2 impaling, Reach C,1. Teeth built to punch through bone and hold.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (13): 4d cutting, Reach C,1. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (11): 4d-1 crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Wing Buffet
attacks.notes: Wing Buffet (11): 4d-2 crushing, Reach C,2. A wing swept across the front arc, using the wings the creature's Flight already pays for. Knocks a lighter target down rather than wounding it. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Acid Breath
attacks.notes: Acid Breath (13): 6d corrosion, Reach Ranged, cone. A cone of acid that catches everything in front of the dragon. It costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, which is the only reason a fight with one lasts more than a turn.

attacks.name: Frightful Presence
attacks.notes: Frightful Presence: Reach Ranged, 20. Everyone who can see the dragon rolls Will. On a failure they are frightened of it and cannot willingly close, and a bad failure means they run. No attack roll and no defence; it costs the dragon nothing.

monsters.name: Adult Brass Dragon
monsters.pageRef: Adult Brass Dragon [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: dragon age and colour variants; answers Adult Brass Dragon (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A sun-warmed ruin half-buried in dune, chosen for the view and the acoustics.

description.text: Brass dragons would genuinely rather talk, and will hold a traveller in conversation for hours before letting them go — or before deciding not to. They are gossips with centuries of material. The breath is fire, and it arrives only once the conversation has failed. An adult has held its territory for centuries, knows every road and every lord in it, and has thought about what to do if adventurers ever came. It is not improvising.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 6d-1 impaling, Reach C,1. Teeth built to punch through bone and hold.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (12): 6d+1 cutting, Reach C,1. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (10): 6d crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Wing Buffet
attacks.notes: Wing Buffet (10): 6d-1 crushing, Reach C,2. A wing swept across the front arc, using the wings the creature's Flight already pays for. Knocks a lighter target down rather than wounding it. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Fire Breath
attacks.notes: Fire Breath (12): 10d burning, Reach Ranged, cone. A cone of fire that catches everything in front of the dragon. It costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, which is the only reason a fight with one lasts more than a turn.

attacks.name: Frightful Presence
attacks.notes: Frightful Presence: Reach Ranged, 20. Everyone who can see the dragon rolls Will. On a failure they are frightened of it and cannot willingly close, and a bad failure means they run. No attack roll and no defence; it costs the dragon nothing.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/brass-dragon-adult.gct
Independent build total: 645 points of racial traits plus 18 points of racial skills.

Answers the SRD heading(s): Adult Brass Dragon (SRD 5.1). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
Body mass used to scale this build: 6000 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
Movement: ground Move 4; air Move 12, 24 at a sprint (primary). The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
Breath damage is stated as literal dice rather than derived from ST: it is a property of the creature's element and age, not of how hard it can push.
The breath is marked as costing fatigue, which halves its contribution to the rating. Without that a dragon would be rated as though it breathed every second, which no dragon does.

Element immunity is built as heavily Limited Damage Resistance rather than as a special rule. It protects against one damage type and nothing else, and it deliberately does not count toward the record's published DR — a red dragon is not armoured against a sword by being immune to fire.

Extra Attack, Frightful Presence, Extended Lifespan, Infravision and the wing buffet were added after a post-hoc comparison against the local Enraged Eggplant dragon conversions and the SRD stat blocks. A dragon that could only act once a turn and could not frighten anyone was not a dragon; the comparison surfaced the gap and the build is still ours.

KNOWN DEFECT in the shared rating path, found by this batch and not worked around here. scripts/review/cer.mjs documents `usesFatigueOrSpell` as halving an attack's contribution, and damageContribution implements it — but combatProfileFromStats never copies the flag onto the profile, so the halving is dead code for damage and live only for afflictions. Sixteen of these forty dragons pick their breath as the best attack and are therefore rated as if they breathed every second. The acid breathers are worst hit, because corrosion carries a x2 damage multiplier: an ancient black dragon rates 227 against an ancient red's 174 on otherwise identical bodies. The fix belongs in cer.mjs and in the application it mirrors, not in these specs. Filed as issue #55 here and Zuljita/DungeonsOnAutomatic#432 in the application; the two must land together, because both implementations share the omission and the parity smoke test therefore passes while both are wrong.
About 9 m nose to tail, which is the SM +4 row.
ST from Basic Lift: it lifts a cart and its team.
Extra Attack: an adult dragon bites and claws in the same turn, which is most of what makes it different from a very large animal.

monsters.name: Ancient Bronze Dragon
monsters.pageRef: Ancient Bronze Dragon [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: dragon age and colour variants; answers Ancient Bronze Dragon (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A sea cave with an underwater entrance, above the tide line and dry inside.

description.text: Bronze dragons haunt coastlines, take an interest in wars they consider just, and have an unnerving habit of turning up in another shape to see what a party is really like. The breath is lightning, and they give warning first. An ancient dragon is older than the kingdom it sleeps under and has outlived everyone who ever knew where it was. It is not a fight. It is a negotiation with something that has already worked out what you want and what you are prepared to trade for it.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (11): 8d-1 impaling, Reach C,1. Teeth built to punch through bone and hold.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (11): 8d+1 cutting, Reach C,1. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (9): 8d crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Wing Buffet
attacks.notes: Wing Buffet (9): 8d-1 crushing, Reach C,2. A wing swept across the front arc, using the wings the creature's Flight already pays for. Knocks a lighter target down rather than wounding it. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Lightning Breath
attacks.notes: Lightning Breath (11): 15d burning, Reach Ranged, cone. A cone of lightning that catches everything in front of the dragon. It costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, which is the only reason a fight with one lasts more than a turn.

attacks.name: Frightful Presence
attacks.notes: Frightful Presence: Reach Ranged, 20. Everyone who can see the dragon rolls Will. On a failure they are frightened of it and cannot willingly close, and a bad failure means they run. No attack roll and no defence; it costs the dragon nothing.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/bronze-dragon-ancient.gct
Independent build total: 760 points of racial traits plus 18 points of racial skills.

Answers the SRD heading(s): Ancient Bronze Dragon (SRD 5.1). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
Body mass used to scale this build: 20000 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
Movement: ground Move 4; air Move 12, 36 at a sprint (primary); water Move 4. The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
Breath damage is stated as literal dice rather than derived from ST: it is a property of the creature's element and age, not of how hard it can push.
The breath is marked as costing fatigue, which halves its contribution to the rating. Without that a dragon would be rated as though it breathed every second, which no dragon does.

Element immunity is built as heavily Limited Damage Resistance rather than as a special rule. It protects against one damage type and nothing else, and it deliberately does not count toward the record's published DR — a red dragon is not armoured against a sword by being immune to fire.

Extra Attack, Frightful Presence, Extended Lifespan, Infravision and the wing buffet were added after a post-hoc comparison against the local Enraged Eggplant dragon conversions and the SRD stat blocks. A dragon that could only act once a turn and could not frighten anyone was not a dragon; the comparison surfaced the gap and the build is still ours.

KNOWN DEFECT in the shared rating path, found by this batch and not worked around here. scripts/review/cer.mjs documents `usesFatigueOrSpell` as halving an attack's contribution, and damageContribution implements it — but combatProfileFromStats never copies the flag onto the profile, so the halving is dead code for damage and live only for afflictions. Sixteen of these forty dragons pick their breath as the best attack and are therefore rated as if they breathed every second. The acid breathers are worst hit, because corrosion carries a x2 damage multiplier: an ancient black dragon rates 227 against an ancient red's 174 on otherwise identical bodies. The fix belongs in cer.mjs and in the application it mirrors, not in these specs. Filed as issue #55 here and Zuljita/DungeonsOnAutomatic#432 in the application; the two must land together, because both implementations share the omission and the parity smoke test therefore passes while both are wrong.
About 15 m nose to tail, which is the SM +5 row, and the point at which the published size discount on Strength has all but bottomed out.
ST from Basic Lift: it lifts a laden wagon in one foot.
Extra Attack: an adult dragon bites and claws in the same turn, which is most of what makes it different from a very large animal.

attacks.name: Bite

attacks.name: Claws

attacks.name: Tail

attacks.name: Wing Buffet

monsters.name: Ancient White Dragon
monsters.pageRef: Ancient White Dragon [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: dragon age and colour variants; answers Ancient White Dragon (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: An ice cave above the snow line, with the hoard frozen into the floor along with the previous claimants.

description.text: White dragons are the smallest and least clever of the chromatic line, and they are pure appetite: they remember slights, they hunt what humiliated them, and they do not plan much beyond that. The breath is a cone of killing cold. An ancient dragon is older than the kingdom it sleeps under and has outlived everyone who ever knew where it was. It is not a fight. It is a negotiation with something that has already worked out what you want and what you are prepared to trade for it.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (11): 8d-1 impaling, Reach C,1. Teeth built to punch through bone and hold.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (11): 8d+1 cutting, Reach C,1. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (9): 8d crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Wing Buffet
attacks.notes: Wing Buffet (9): 8d-1 crushing, Reach C,2. A wing swept across the front arc, using the wings the creature's Flight already pays for. Knocks a lighter target down rather than wounding it. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Cold Breath
attacks.notes: Cold Breath (11): 15d burning, Reach Ranged, cone. A cone of freezing cold that catches everything in front of the dragon. It costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, which is the only reason a fight with one lasts more than a turn.

attacks.name: Frightful Presence
attacks.notes: Frightful Presence: Reach Ranged, 20. Everyone who can see the dragon rolls Will. On a failure they are frightened of it and cannot willingly close, and a bad failure means they run. No attack roll and no defence; it costs the dragon nothing.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/white-dragon-ancient.gct
Independent build total: 755 points of racial traits plus 18 points of racial skills.

Answers the SRD heading(s): Ancient White Dragon (SRD 5.1). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
Body mass used to scale this build: 20000 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
Movement: ground Move 4; air Move 12, 36 at a sprint (primary). The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
Breath damage is stated as literal dice rather than derived from ST: it is a property of the creature's element and age, not of how hard it can push.
The breath is marked as costing fatigue, which halves its contribution to the rating. Without that a dragon would be rated as though it breathed every second, which no dragon does.

Element immunity is built as heavily Limited Damage Resistance rather than as a special rule. It protects against one damage type and nothing else, and it deliberately does not count toward the record's published DR — a red dragon is not armoured against a sword by being immune to fire.

Extra Attack, Frightful Presence, Extended Lifespan, Infravision and the wing buffet were added after a post-hoc comparison against the local Enraged Eggplant dragon conversions and the SRD stat blocks. A dragon that could only act once a turn and could not frighten anyone was not a dragon; the comparison surfaced the gap and the build is still ours.

KNOWN DEFECT in the shared rating path, found by this batch and not worked around here. scripts/review/cer.mjs documents `usesFatigueOrSpell` as halving an attack's contribution, and damageContribution implements it — but combatProfileFromStats never copies the flag onto the profile, so the halving is dead code for damage and live only for afflictions. Sixteen of these forty dragons pick their breath as the best attack and are therefore rated as if they breathed every second. The acid breathers are worst hit, because corrosion carries a x2 damage multiplier: an ancient black dragon rates 227 against an ancient red's 174 on otherwise identical bodies. The fix belongs in cer.mjs and in the application it mirrors, not in these specs. Filed as issue #55 here and Zuljita/DungeonsOnAutomatic#432 in the application; the two must land together, because both implementations share the omission and the parity smoke test therefore passes while both are wrong.
About 15 m nose to tail, which is the SM +5 row, and the point at which the published size discount on Strength has all but bottomed out.
ST from Basic Lift: it lifts a laden wagon in one foot.
Extra Attack: an adult dragon bites and claws in the same turn, which is most of what makes it different from a very large animal.

description.text: Grey, hairless dwarves who kept the craft and lost everything else. Duergar work mines with slave labour, resent every hour of it, and are joyless in a way that reads as menace long before anyone draws. They can simply stop being visible, which they do without ceremony and usually about four seconds before it matters.

attacks.notes: War Pick (12): 1d+2 impaling, Reach 1. Punched through mail. Duergar generally open the fight already invisible and standing closer than anyone believed possible.

attacks.name: Shield Bash
attacks.notes: Shield Bash (12): 1d-1 crushing, Reach 1. Used to pin somebody against the gallery wall while the pick works.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/duergar.gct

monsters.lair: Whatever was standing there before the pack arrived, now roofless and stinking.

description.text: Hyena-headed raiders who hunt in packs and take the long way round to get behind you. Gnolls follow a scent for days, are audibly delighted by a fight going their way, and stop to eat before the fight is properly over — which is the only mercy anyone gets from them. A camp they have passed through is recognisable from a distance by the smell.

attacks.notes: Battleaxe (12): 2d+1 cutting, Reach 1. Taken off somebody, kept badly, and still perfectly effective.

attacks.name: Bite

attacks.name: Shortbow
attacks.notes: Shortbow (11): 1d+1 impaling, Reach Ranged, 100. Loosed at anything running away. The damage is the bow's.

One goblin is a nuisance and runs at the first real hit; twelve of them in a tunnel they dug, with spears and a hole in the ceiling, are a serious afternoon. attacks.notes: Shortsword (12): 1d-1 cutting, Reach 1. Notched, too big for the hand holding it, and swung anyway.

attacks.name: Spear
attacks.notes: Spear (12): 1d-1 impaling, Reach 1,2. The one goblin weapon that works, because it lets them fight three deep from behind each other.

attacks.name: Shortbow
attacks.notes: Shortbow (11): 1d+1 impaling, Reach Ranged, 100. Loosed in volleys from a gallery nobody looked up at. The damage is the bow's.

monsters.name: Hobgoblin
monsters.pageRef: Hobgoblin [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Hobgoblin (SRD 5.1); Hobgoblin (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A fort with cleared ground in front of it, a watch roster, and a gate that is actually shut.

description.text: The goblinoid that got organised. Hobgoblins drill, post sentries, hold a line when it is losing and rotate the front rank while doing it — which makes six of them a harder problem than twenty goblins and a considerably worse surprise. They are not frightened of adventurers. They have a standing plan for adventurers.

attacks.name: Longsword
attacks.notes: Longsword (13): 1d+3 cutting, Reach 1. Drilled with, maintained, and used in a line with somebody else's shield on the flank.

attacks.name: Shield Bash
attacks.notes: Shield Bash (13): 1d-1 crushing, Reach 1. The line steps forward together. This is what steps forward first.

attacks.name: Longbow
attacks.notes: Longbow (12): 1d+2 impaling, Reach Ranged, 200. Volleyed on command from the rank behind. The damage is the bow's.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/hobgoblin.gct
Independent build total: 79 points of racial traits plus 22 points of racial skills.

Answers the SRD heading(s): Hobgoblin (SRD 5.1); Hobgoblin (SRD 3.5). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
Body mass used to scale this build: 90 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary). The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
About 1.9 m standing, which is the SM 0 row.
ST 12 from Basic Lift: a soldier's frame carrying a soldier's load all day.
Combat Reflexes and Fearlessness are the record. A hobgoblin without them is an orc in better kit, and the whole reason the creature exists is that it does not break.

Mail and a shield are standard issue and are not in this record's DR. This is the record in the batch where that decision costs the most, and it is stated rather than quietly compensated for. See decision 11 in the build policy.

monsters.name: Kobold
monsters.pageRef: Kobold [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Kobold (SRD 5.1); Kobold (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A mine they dug themselves, in which every third corridor is a mistake to walk down.

description.text: Knee-high scaled things with dog-like snouts, and by some distance the best military engineers in any dungeon. A kobold in a fair fight is nothing at all. Kobolds do not have fair fights: they have pits, deadfalls, thirty of themselves and a corridor they know the safe route through. Cold makes them slow and daylight makes them wretched.

attacks.name: Spear
attacks.notes: Spear (12): 1d-2 impaling, Reach 1,2. Held at the far end and used from behind whatever is in the way.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 1d-4 cutting, Reach C. What is left when the spear has been dropped and the corridor is full.

attacks.name: Sling
attacks.notes: Sling (11): 1d-3 crushing, Reach Ranged, 60. From a ledge, in the dark, at a party already dealing with something else.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/kobold.gct
Independent build total: -14 points of racial traits plus 26 points of racial skills.

Answers the SRD heading(s): Kobold (SRD 5.1); Kobold (SRD 3.5). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
Body mass used to scale this build: 20 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary). The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
About 0.9 m standing, which is the SM -2 row.
ST 7: the weakest folk in this batch. Everything dangerous about a kobold happens before the fight starts.
Cold-Blooded is bought at published cost. Kobolds are reptiles and a cold gallery genuinely slows them down, which is worth a GM knowing.

The traps are not built as attacks on this record. A pit is terrain the kobold made, not a thing the kobold does in a turn, and putting it on the stat block would rate every individual kobold as though it carried the whole mine around.

monsters.name: Lizardfolk
monsters.pageRef: Lizardfolk [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Lizardfolk (SRD 5.1); Lizardfolk (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A village of stilt huts over black water, reached by a channel only a flat boat clears.

description.text: Scaled, tailed and entirely at home in water a person would drown in. Lizardfolk hunt from below, hold their breath for minutes at a stretch, and come up under a boat rather than alongside it. They are not cruel and not much interested in anyone's business, which lasts exactly as long as nobody hunts their stretch of the marsh.

attacks.name: Barbed Spear
attacks.notes: Barbed Spear (11): 1d+2 impaling, Reach 1,2. Fire-hardened, barbed for fish and entirely adequate for the other thing.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C. Delivered in the water, on something already being held under.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (10): 1d crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc at knee height. Cannot parry.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/lizardfolk.gct
Independent build total: 49 points of racial traits plus 22 points of racial skills.

Answers the SRD heading(s): Lizardfolk (SRD 5.1); Lizardfolk (SRD 3.5). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
Body mass used to scale this build: 90 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary); water Move 5. The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
About 1.9 m standing, which is the SM 0 row; the tail behind that is reach rather than height.
ST 13 from Basic Lift: it poles a laden boat and drags a deer-sized kill through mud.

DR 2 is genuine scale and is bought as Tough Skin, so a scratch that only needs skin contact gets through it. That is the right shape for hide rather than for armour, and it is the only DR in this record.

monsters.name: Merfolk
monsters.pageRef: Merfolk [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Merfolk (SRD 5.1); Merfolk (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A reef terrace or a drowned harbour wall, built on rather than into.

description.text: People from the waist up and something with a tail below it, living on reefs and in drowned places and perfectly willing to talk to a ship that behaves itself. Merfolk breathe air and water equally, which is why negotiations happen at the rail rather than underwater. On land they can drag themselves about, and they hate every moment of it.

attacks.name: Trident
attacks.notes: Trident (12): 1d+2 impaling, Reach 1,2. Held two-handed and driven upward, which is the direction merfolk fight from.

attacks.name: Thrown Spear
attacks.notes: Thrown Spear (12): 1d impaling, Reach Ranged, 15. Thrown through water at short range, where a bow would be useless.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/merfolk.gct
Independent build total: 73 points of racial traits plus 14 points of racial skills.

Answers the SRD heading(s): Merfolk (SRD 5.1); Merfolk (SRD 3.5). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
Body mass used to scale this build: 90 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
Movement: ground Move 5; water Move 5 (primary). The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
About 2.1 m nose to tail-tip, which reads on the SM 0 row.
ST 11: a swimmer's build, strong through the back and shoulders and no use at all for carrying anything up a beach.

Breathing is built as Doesn't Breathe with the published Oxygen Absorption limitation rather than as Gills. Gills would say a merfolk suffocates in air, and the whole encounter value of the creature is that it does not.

No Legs (Aquatic) prices at zero, as it does for the fish in the aquatic batch. The ground Move the movement note reports is the builder's floor, not a walk: out of water a merfolk hauls itself along at a fraction of it and should be run that way.

monsters.name: Merrow
monsters.pageRef: Merrow [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Merrow (SRD 5.1); Merrow (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A flooded sea cave with a shingle shelf at the back, and bones on the shelf.

description.text: Ogres that went into the sea and got worse. A merrow is three metres of green-grey muscle with a harpoon and a rope, and its whole method is to put the barb into somebody at the rail and pull. They are not clever, they are patient in the way an ambush predator is patient, and a shipwrecked party is exactly the situation they wait for.

attacks.name: Harpoon
attacks.notes: Harpoon (10): 2d+2 impaling, Reach 1,2. Barbed and roped. Being hit by it is the smaller half of the problem.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (11): 2d-2 cutting, Reach C. Taken while the harpoon rope is still being hauled.

attacks.name: Slam
attacks.notes: Slam (10): 2d-1 crushing, Reach C,1. Delivered from below with the whole mass behind it, in water, where nobody has footing.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/merrow.gct
Independent build total: 84 points of racial traits plus 10 points of racial skills.

Answers the SRD heading(s): Merrow (SRD 5.1); Merrow (SRD 3.5). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
Body mass used to scale this build: 300 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
Movement: ground Move 5; water Move 5 (primary). The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
About 2.7 m, which is the SM +1 row; the published Strength discount for size applies at -10%.
ST 20 from Basic Lift and from the job: it hauls an armoured man off a deck and under.
Amphibious and Oxygen Absorption together, like the merfolk: it fights in the water, drags prey into the water, and can follow onto a beach without inconvenience.
DR 2 is hide. A merrow wears nothing, so this is the one record among the armed folk here where the published DR is the whole story.

monsters.name: Mountain Dwarf
monsters.pageRef: Mountain Dwarf [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Mountain Dwarf (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A hold cut into a valley wall, with the forge at the front and the mine behind it.

description.text: The dwarves who stayed where the sun still reaches: hold-builders, smiths and by inclination soldiers. A mountain dwarf sees warm bodies in an unlit gallery, walks all day under a load that would fell a taller man, and holds a grudge with the same steady competence it brings to everything else. They fight in ranks and they do not give ground.

attacks.name: Warhammer
attacks.notes: Warhammer (12): 1d+4 crushing, Reach 1. Made at the forge it was carried out of, and heavier than it looks in that hand.

attacks.name: Dwarven Axe
attacks.notes: Dwarven Axe (12): 1d+3 cutting, Reach 1. The other half of the same argument.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/mountain-dwarf.gct

monsters.pageRef: Ogre [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Ogre (SRD 5.1); Ogre (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A cave with a fire outside it and the remains of several carts scattered downhill.

description.text: Three metres of appetite with a club. Ogres are slow, stupid, foul-tempered and enormously strong, and the arithmetic of a fight with one is simple: it will hit somebody eventually, and when it does that person stops being a combatant. They take toll on roads, eat what they take, and are not open to a second offer.

attacks.name: Greatclub
attacks.notes: Greatclub (10): 3d+5 crushing, Reach 1,2. A tree limb with a stone lashed into the end. It arrives slowly and it does not matter.

attacks.name: Javelin
attacks.notes: Javelin (10): 2d impaling, Reach Ranged, 20. A sharpened fence rail, thrown downhill at whoever is fastest.

attacks.name: Fist
attacks.notes: Fist (11): 2d-1 crushing, Reach C,1. What happens when the club is on the wrong side of the fight.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/ogre.gct

Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
About 2.9 m standing, which is the SM +1 row; Strength carries the published -10% size discount.

monsters.lair: A house in a mountain village where the previous family is not discussed.

description.text: An ogre with a sorcerer's education and centuries of practice at pretending to be somebody's neighbour. In its own shape it is a horned, blue-skinned giant with a glaive; in the shape it usually wears it is a well-liked man in a mountain village. It flies, it vanishes, it heals what you do to it, and it would rather charm the guard than fight the party.

attacks.name: Glaive
attacks.notes: Glaive (13): 4d+3 cutting, Reach 1,2. Kept on the wall of the house it took, and reached for without changing shape first.

attacks.name: Cone of Cold
attacks.notes: Cone of Cold (14): 6d burning, Reach Ranged, cone. A breath of killing cold across the front arc. It costs the oni to use and cannot be repeated every second.

attacks.name: Charm
attacks.notes: Charm: Reach Ranged, 10. One person is told to stop, and rolls against Will to not. The oni much prefers this to the glaive, because a charmed guard opens the door.

monsters.lair: A stockade round a stolen village, or a gallery in somebody else's mine.

description.text: Broad, grey-skinned and permanently furious, orcs raid because raiding is the shape their society has settled into and because they enjoy it. They come in numbers, they close immediately, and they keep coming after the point where a sensible band would have withdrawn. Daylight leaves them squinting, which is why the attack is nearly always at dusk.

attacks.name: Javelin
attacks.notes: Javelin (11): 1d+1 impaling, Reach Ranged, 20. Thrown once at the charge, then forgotten about.

attacks.name: Fist
attacks.notes: Fist (11): 1d crushing, Reach C. Used on other orcs about as often as on anyone else.

monsters.lair: A clearing nobody finds twice, somewhere in old wood.

description.text: A hand-span of winged fey with a bow and no fear whatsoever. A sprite can simply stop being visible, hovers where nothing can reach it, and knows the wood better than anything walking through it. Its arrows do no damage worth the name and put people to sleep where they stand, which is a far worse outcome than being shot.

attacks.name: Sprite Bow
attacks.notes: Sprite Bow (16): 1d-4 impaling, Reach Ranged, 40. The arrow is the size of a pin and the wound is nothing. What is on the point puts a grown soldier to sleep for an hour.

attacks.name: Needle Sword
attacks.notes: Needle Sword (15): 1d-6 impaling, Reach C. Genuinely a threat only to something the sprite's own size, and drawn with complete confidence regardless.

notes: GCS ancestry draft: gcs/sprite.gct

description.text: Somebody with a fiend somewhere in the family, and everybody can tell. Tieflings run to horns, unsettling eyes and a tail they keep under a coat, and they spend their lives being blamed first. attacks.notes: Horrifying Visage (14): 1d-4 toxic, Reach Ranged, gaze. The face it wears when it stops pretending to be what it was. A Fright Check at penalty; those who fail are staggered by terror, and the young can be aged by it.

monsters.lair: A defended household with money, staff who do not ask, and a windowless room nobody mentions.

description.text: A predator that owns property. It passes for a living aristocrat as long as it feeds carefully, and the household around it exists to make the feeding careful. Sunlight burns it and it knows every hour of the almanac; the fight you get is the one it prepared, at night, indoors, on its ground.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (16): 1d+1 impaling, Reach C. Delivered to a grappled or willing victim. The wound is small; the draining is not, and a victim held through it loses blood by the round.

attacks.name: Slam
attacks.notes: Slam (16): 1d+3 crushing, Reach C,1. Strength far past what the frame suggests.

attacks.name: Dominating Gaze
attacks.notes: Dominating Gaze (16): 1d-4 toxic, Reach Ranged, gaze. Meet its eyes and resist with Will or do as you are told and remember agreeing to it. It prefers this to violence; violence is noisy.

monsters.lair: A tower, tomb or buried library arranged for the convenience of one scholar and the death of visitors, with its true treasure hidden somewhere else entirely.

description.text: A wizard who solved dying and kept working. Everything about the encounter was decided before you arrived: the approach, the ambush, which of you it wants alive to question. attacks.notes: Paralyzing Touch (15): 1d toxic, Reach C. A hand like winter through the armor's gaps. Resist with HT or the body simply stops answering, and the lich walks past you to the one it actually came for.

attacks.name: Deathly Bolt
attacks.notes: Deathly Bolt (16): 6d burning, Reach Ranged. Stated as literal dice: the bolt is a property of the lich's art, not its arm. It costs the creature to cast, and a lich in its own lair has cheaper ways to spend you first.

attacks.name: Frightening Gaze
attacks.notes: Frightening Gaze (15): 1d-4 toxic, Reach Ranged, gaze. The attention of something that has already outlived your grandchildren. Fright Check at penalty; it uses this on the brave first.

monsters.lair: The tomb complex it was interred to rule, with its organs in jars in a chamber it defends above its own body.

description.text: The buried king still holding court. attacks.notes: Rotting Fist (12): 2d crushing, Reach C,1. The blow lands like a club, and what it leaves behind is worse: resist with HT or take the rot, a curse under the skin. Wounds will not close and healing arts fail until the curse itself is lifted.

attacks.name: Dreadful Glare
attacks.notes: Dreadful Glare (12): 1d-4 toxic, Reach Ranged, gaze. The tomb's own verdict on trespass. Fright Check at penalty; a badly failed roll leaves the victim paralyzed by dread as it closes.

monsters.lair: A scraped burrow under a slab, with the sand outside smoothed by its own passage.

description.text: Two and a half metres of black chitin that holds you with the claws and takes its time with the tail. The shell turns most weapons, the pincers do not let go, and the sting is what actually kills — everything before it is the scorpion arranging matters to its satisfaction.

attacks.name: Sting
attacks.notes: Sting (13): 1d+2 impaling, Reach C,1. Arched over the back and driven down. Roll HT or the limb goes numb, then the chest does; a second sting on a failed victim is usually the end of it.

attacks.name: Pincer
attacks.notes: Pincer (13): 1d+1 cutting, Reach C,1. Grabs and holds the target still for the sting. Cannot parry.

ST from Basic Lift: it drags a human body into a burrow.

Rating caveat for review: the giant spider out-rates this creature, which is not obviously right. The cause is in the rating path, not the build — a binding is scored at its raw ST while a disabling ability is scored at one point per five, so the spider's web (ST 16) contributes 16 while this scorpion's lethal venom (30 points) contributes 6. Only the better of the two is counted per creature, so the spider's own venom is also discarded. Recorded rather than tuned around; the fix belongs in the CER path.
Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Spider
monsters.pageRef: Giant Spider [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: vermin and monstrous arthropods; answers Giant Spider (SRD 5.1); Monstrous Spider (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A sheet of web strung across a shaft or a stand of trees, with wrapped bundles hanging in it.

description.text: A body the size of a large dog on a three-metre span of legs, sitting motionless at the edge of its web where the light does not reach. It reads the whole web as one sense. What it wants is for you to be held still, and it has already arranged most of that before anybody looks up.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (15): 1d impaling, Reach C. Delivered to something already wrapped. Roll HT or go slack — the venom is meant to stop prey struggling, not to kill it outright.

attacks.name: Web
attacks.notes: Web: Reach 5. Thrown as a sheet from ambush. No damage; the target is stuck fast and must win a Quick Contest against the web's ST to tear free, and everything the spider does afterwards is against a target that cannot move. The web itself has DR 3 and can be cut or burned free; fire clears a hex of it in a turn and is by far the fastest answer.
